terms.grammar: adjective, comparative of bonus (bonus, melior, optimus); genitive meliōris
evidence: Hor. S. 1.5.96: postera tempestās melior, via pejor
Liv. 30.30.19: melior tūtiorque est certa pāx quam spērāta victōria
terms.comment: “Better than” is quam or the ablative: quid melius Rōmā?, what is better than Rome? (Ov. Pont. 1.3.37).

terms.grammar: adverb, comparative of bene (bene, melius, optimē)

terms.gloss: it is better to, one had better
terms.grammar: phrase, with an infinitive; often with quam
evidence: Ter. Ad. 57–58: satius esse crēdō quam metū
Plin. Ep. 1.9.8: satius est enim … ōtiōsum esse quam nihil agere
terms.comment: The comparative of satis: “more satisfactory, preferable” (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: the next day the weather was better, the road worse

phrases.latin: Pudōre et līberālitāte līberōs retinēre satius esse crēdō quam metū.
phrases.english: I think it better to keep children in hand by a sense of honour and by kindness than by fear.

sources: Lewis & Short: melior · Lewis & Short: bonus · Lewis & Short: melius · Lewis & Short: satis
